decision.rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm), so a direct-match exists. PGS000753 is preferred because it is from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) with a clearly stated AAA endpoint (prevalent AAA), basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and it reports a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), which provides direct evidence of PRS signal without relying on covariate-boosted full-model discrimination. The main limitation is that several other direct-match models use genome-wide shrinkage methods (PRS-CS/LDpred2/shaPRS) and/or report full-model AUROC/C-index, but the context does not provide PRS-only AUROC for them and their reported full-model metrics are not directly comparable; additionally, some have unknown covariates. This makes it hard to confidently identify a single clearly best-performing PRS from the metadata alone, so confidence is moderate and the outcome is sub-optimal rather than high-quality.

All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target trait alcohol dependence via alcohol use disorder / problematic alcohol use, with phenotype fields aligning to AUD (DSM-5 criteria count or AUD diagnosis) and EFO mappings to alcohol dependence/alcohol dependence measurement. Among them, PGS002738 is the most directly aligned on concept (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder) and provides the strongest visible discriminative evidence via an OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900), which is more interpretable for case/control risk stratification than the small ΔR² values reported for PGS000201/PGS000202. Main limitation: none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², covariates are unknown for PGS002738 (reducing comparability), and PGS000201/PGS000202 use a DSM-5 criteria-count endpoint (continuous) rather than a binary dependence diagnosis, so the evidence is not sufficient to call a clearly high-quality winner.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned endpoints. PGS001777 is preferred because it is disease-focused (alcohol-related cirrhosis in drinkers) and provides the strongest PRS-specific discrimination evidence in the visible metadata via a large risk gradient (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18, 95% CI 4.05–9.41), whereas PGS000704 reports only a modest per-SD HR (1.18) and a full-model C-index (0.711) that is not PRS-only, and PGS004913 reports modest variance explained (R² = 0.029) without a clearly PRS-only discrimination metric. Main limitation: none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only AUROC, and PGS001777 has unknown covariates and a small validation sample (n=1,390) with a male-only phenotype note, which reduces certainty despite the strong OR evidence.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with generally aligned endpoints (Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, the snpnet UKB model PGS001261 (Angina pectoris time-to-event) reports explicit PGS-only performance (PGS AUROC 0.58233; PGS R2 0.01228) plus incremental AUROC (0.00796) with basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and EUR validation, making it more comparable than candidates that only report full-model C-index/AUROC or only an OR. PGS001262 has higher full-model AUROC (0.80729) but similarly modest PGS-only AUROC/R2, suggesting the high AUROC is largely covariate-driven; PGS000703 lacks PRS-only metrics; PGS004457/PGS004527 report only OR with unknown covariates; and the MVP benchmarking set (PGS005048 etc.) reports only full-model C-index/OR without PRS-only metrics, limiting comparability. Limitation: evidence remains sub-optimal because the strongest-looking discrimination numbers in several alternatives are full-model metrics (not PRS-only), and the chosen model’s PRS-only signal is modest and from a pan-trait UKB framework paper, which domain guidance flags as potentially less reliable for external generalization.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. Two candidates (PGS001267/PGS001268) come from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as prone to poorer external generalization despite having explicit PRS-only AUROC/R²; one is also time-to-event (PGS001268), adding endpoint packaging complexity. The remaining UKB portability-family candidates (PGS001876, PGS002089) have endpoint-aligned phenotyping and cleaner/basic covariates, but report only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R²), limiting comparability; among them, PGS002089 has the stronger reported partial-r (0.0919 vs 0.0797) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with many variants (22,026), making it the best-supported choice within the non-framework set. East Asian-only Taiwanese models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation (n=1,298), so their AUROC is not reliably comparable as PRS-only evidence. Overall, evidence is sufficient to prefer PGS002089, but confidence is capped because key PRS-comparable metrics are missing for the portability-family models and the strongest explicit PRS-only metrics come from a framework paper that is penalized by domain guidance.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is explicitly aligned to the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo: aortic stenosis) with endpoint-faithful phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with a large variant set (1,119,377), and provides a representative discrimination metric in European evaluation (C-index 0.87) plus a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92). The main limitation is that the reported 0.87 is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariate adjustment (multiple comorbidities and risk factors) and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; competing direct-match models (e.g., PGS005254) report HRs but lack comparable discrimination metrics, leaving some residual uncertainty.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)", trait_efo=arthritis) and two "Other arthritis" models (PGS004477, PGS004547; trait_efo=arthritis). PGS001135 is the most endpoint-faithful to the generic target (phenotyping_reported="Arthritis (nos)") and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus incremental AUROC (0.00314), enabling interpretation beyond full-model discrimination. However, it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk, and its PRS-only signal is modest. The alternative exact-EFO arthritis models (PGS004477/PGS004547) lack comparable discrimination metrics (only an OR is shown and covariates are unknown), making them harder to justify as clearly stronger despite being direct matches. Therefore a direct match exists but evidence is insufficient for a high-quality, unambiguous recommendation.

Direct-match asthma PRS candidates are present (many models with trait_efo=asthma). Among the visible set, PGS001344 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity for generic asthma risk (phenotyping_reported: "Asthma diagnosed by doctor"), uses only basic demographic/technical covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and reports comparatively strong and PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64568; PGS-only R2=0.05973; full-model AUROC=0.66621; incremental AUROC=0.07977) with a reasonably large European validation sample (n=19,857). Competing candidates either come from pan-trait/framework or portability-style studies (e.g., snpnet 813-traits; UKB portability), have weaker/less comparable performance reporting (many report only full-model AUROC or only incremental R2), have endpoint restrictions (pediatric/childhood asthma), or have heavier/non-PRS covariate packaging (e.g., family/environmental risk scores). The main limitation is that several other direct-match models show similar performance signals but are not directly comparable due to differing endpoints/metrics (e.g., PRS-CS-auto/global biobank models with AUROC but unclear PGS-only AUROC; multi-ancestry pediatric asthma with strong OR but pediatric endpoint), so the choice is supported but not uniquely decisive from the provided metadata alone.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (atopic eczema). However, several have endpoint mismatches: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis (therapy-specific), and PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (severity-restricted) with a small validation sample (n=676) and only full-model metrics (AUROC 0.93, R² 0.49) that are not PRS-only and appear implausibly high relative to the provided heritability ceiling, suggesting covariate-driven performance. Among the remaining endpoint-faithful incident atopic dermatitis models, PGS002755 (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants) provides the strongest structural PRS signal (genome-wide shrinkage) with a large European evaluation (n=337,910) and a reported HR (high vs low PRS) of 1.249 (1.123–1.391). PGS004587 is also incident AD but uses only 23 GWAS-significant SNPs and shows a weaker HR (1.153). Confidence is limited because none of the incident-AD candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², and the available effect sizes are not directly comparable across studies.

Multiple direct-match atrial fibrillation PRS candidates are present. PGS005168 is best supported in this context because it is a disease-focused, multi-cohort atrial fibrillation PRS (Nat Genet 2025; meta-analysis >180,000 cases) with endpoint-aligned phenotyping_reported ('Atrial fibrillation') and strong reported discrimination in its selected European validation record (C-index 0.8718 with CI 0.8657–0.878) plus a per-SD effect size (HR 1.6663; β 0.5106). Competing candidates either come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., UKB sparse/portability papers), use horizon-conditioned or risk-calculator packaging (e.g., CHARGE-AF/5-year risk models), or provide weaker/less comparable performance evidence (often only full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics). Main limitation: the reported C-index appears to be a full-model metric with covariates including CHARGE-AF (a named clinical risk calculator), which domain guidance flags as risk-wrapper packaging that can inflate discrimination and reduces comparability to standalone PRS; PRS-only AUROC/R2 is not provided here, so confidence is not High.

All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (atrial flutter appears explicitly in trait_reported/trait_efo for PGS001263 and in the combined AF/flutter endpoints for PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050). PGS001263 is preferred because it is the only model with an atrial-flutter-specific endpoint (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both 'Atrial flutter') and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.61716; PGS R2 no covariates=0.02517), which are interpretable and below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), supporting metric sanity. Main limitation: the strongest endpoint-specific option comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework ('across 813 traits', snpnet), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable for external generalization; additionally, the competing portability-study models (PGS001841/PGS002050) use a closely related combined AF/flutter phenotype but lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, making cross-candidate performance comparison incomplete and lowering confidence.

Both candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (autism spectrum disorder), but PGS000327 has clearly stronger endpoint fidelity and more coherent disease-focused evidence. PGS000327’s phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder,” whereas PGS002790’s phenotyping_reported is “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn),” creating an endpoint mismatch despite the ASD label. On performance evidence, PGS000327 reports an OR per SD of 1.33 (moderate signal) and an R² metric (0.0245) from a single European validation record; PGS002790 reports only a small partial R² (~0.00546) with no effect sizes, and its many performance records do not compensate for the phenotype misalignment per the provided domain guidance. Both are EUR-only in evaluation, so ancestry does not differentiate. Main limitation: neither model provides PRS-only AUROC/PRS-only R² explicitly, so absolute comparability of the reported R²/partial R² remains somewhat uncertain, but the endpoint alignment advantage makes PGS000327 the best-supported direct-match choice.

All listed candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_reported/trait_efo. Prioritizing endpoint fidelity and comparable performance evidence, PGS000452 has clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and the strongest visible discrimination/effect evidence among the pool: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647) with a strong per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761) and top-1% vs rest OR 3.61 (2.53–5.15), plus the highest reported Nagelkerke R² (0.0487) among the Cancer PRSweb siblings. Close competitors (e.g., PGS000454 and PGS000456) have essentially similar AUROC/OR but do not clearly exceed PGS000452 on the visible metrics, while newer Nat Commun 2023 models (PGS003416/PGS003417) and the 2025 survivor-specific model (PGS005207) lack comparable AUROC/R² and/or have less endpoint-general phenotyping (keratinocyte cancers; childhood cancer survivors). Confidence is Moderate because most candidates report only full-model AUROC (not PGS-only metrics), making cross-model performance comparability limited and leaving several near-tied siblings.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. PGS000924 is a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework score ("across 813 traits"; snpnet; 5 variants) with time-to-event phenotyping and unusually high reported R2/AUROC relative to the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.089), which raises comparability/optimism concerns per the domain guidance. PGS001824 and PGS002032 are endpoint-faithful ("Disorders of bilirubin excretion"; trait_efo=bilirubin metabolism disease) and come from the same portability study with identical reported partial-r (~0.0716) and similar covariates; they lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, limiting discrimination between them. Between these two near-clones, PGS002032 is modestly preferred on structural grounds (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 19,768 variants vs penalized regression with 22 variants) given no conflicting performance evidence. Main limitation: the key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) are missing for the preferred model, so confidence cannot be high.

All three candidates are direct trait matches within the bipolar spectrum (PGS002786: bipolar disorder; PGS002787: bipolar I; PGS002788: bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, similar variant counts (~935k–949k), and similar small reported partial R² values (~0.0025–0.0031). However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly mismatched because each model’s phenotyping_reported refers to non-diagnosis outcomes (cognitive/behavioral measures) rather than bipolar disorder case-control status, which is a major limitation for selecting a bipolar-disorder PRS. Given the target is broad ‘bipolar disorder’, PGS002786 is the closest concept match (trait_reported/trait_efo) and has the largest variant count among the siblings, but the evidence is insufficient to call any option high-quality for the target endpoint.

All three candidates are direct matches at the broad level of the target concept (blood coagulation disease), but none is a clearly high-quality, endpoint-faithful, disease-focused PRS from the visible metadata. PGS001033 maps directly to the target EFO (blood coagulation disease) and provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.634) and PGS-only R² (0.0578) with only basic covariates, which is stronger comparable-performance evidence than the other two models. However, it is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ('across 813 traits') and is extremely sparse (1 variant) with a time-to-event phenotype, both of which are warning signals for generalizability. The two alternatives (PGS001826, PGS002034) are for a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO (not the broad blood coagulation disease target) and come from a portability framework paper with only partial-correlation metrics (no AUROC/R²), making them hard to compare and not clearly better supported. Given these limitations and competing endpoint mismatches/framework penalties, the best choice is only weakly supported.

Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant in the provided context (multiple models with trait_efo=breast carcinoma / phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer). Among the visible candidates, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: Breast cancer), reports comparatively strong discrimination in its selected European validation record (full_model AUROC=0.6625 with accompanying OR=1.83 and R²=0.0764), and uses no non-genetic covariates (covariates=0), reducing concern that performance is driven by clinical risk-factor packaging. A key limitation is that many other direct-match models are also well-aligned and some report higher AUROC in different settings (e.g., PGS000007 full_model AUROC=0.78 but with age/sex covariates and a different study family), and most models lack clearly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R²; therefore, while PGS004153 is a defensible best pick from the visible evidence, the choice is not uniquely decisive, keeping confidence at Moderate.

All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease by trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and in whether reported performance is PRS-comparable. PGS000316 has a clean, direct endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease), is not from a pan-trait/portability framework paper, and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.879 with CI) with very large validation (n=379,767), making it the most broadly supported disease-focused option in the provided set. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as Unknown (no PGS-only AUROC/R²), so comparability to other scores’ PRS-only metrics is uncertain; this prevents a high-confidence ‘best’ designation despite being the strongest overall evidence package among the direct-match candidates.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is preferred because it comes from a cervical-phenotype-focused GWAS meta-analysis study (“GWAS meta-analyses clarify genetics of cervical phenotypes and inform risk stratification for cervical cancer”) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred; ~2.9M variants), which is structurally stronger than sparse/GWAS-hit scores when endpoint alignment is comparable. It also reports a moderate per-SD effect size (HR=1.33) with basic covariates (age, smoking), supporting non-trivial PRS signal. However, confidence is limited because most candidates report only full-model discrimination (C-index/AUROC) rather than clearly PRS-only metrics, and the reported full-model C-index for PGS003428 (0.613) is not directly comparable to other models’ full-model metrics given differing covariate sets; additionally, some alternatives have similar endpoint fidelity and large validations (e.g., PGS000073/PGS000784) but are GWAS-hit style with weaker standalone-PRS interpretability from the provided metrics.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis, but most come from pan-trait/framework-style UKB efforts (PGS001174: “813 traits” sparse snpnet; PGS001861/PGS002072: “Portability of 245 polygenic scores”) which domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable than disease-focused models when a disease-focused alternative exists. The two Commun Biol 2024 models (PGS004476 LDpred2; PGS004546 RFDiseasemetaPRS) are endpoint-faithful (ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis) and appear disease-focused (risk-factor + disease PRS integration), and they provide per-SD effect size evidence; among them, PGS004546 reports the stronger OR (1.2986 vs 1.2194), making it the better-supported sibling given otherwise similar metadata (same cohorts, ancestry, variant count, validation size). Main limitation: these 2024 models lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) and list covariates as Unknown, so the strength of evidence is incomplete and prevents a high-confidence selection.

Multiple direct-match CKD models are present. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD-focused (Nat Med: “Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”), uses a clear CKD stage ≥3 definition via eGFR <45 (high endpoint fidelity for CKD), and shows strong reported discrimination in validation (full-model AUROC 0.78 with an OR 1.47). It also includes multi-ancestry evaluation, supporting transportability relative to EUR-only evaluations. Main limitation: the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use, etc.), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be directly compared across candidates; this keeps confidence at Moderate despite strong disease-focused evidence.

Multiple direct-match COPD candidates are present (PGS001332/133/134/1783/1788/1850/2062/4466/4536). Among these, PGS001783 is a direct phenotype match (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease”, trait_efo matches), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto; 884,139 variants), and comes from a large multi-biobank development context (many contributing cohorts listed), which domain guidance treats as structurally stronger than pan-trait sparse UKB framework scores (PGS001332/133/134) and UKB portability sweeps (PGS001850/002062). It also reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092), providing more directly interpretable PRS signal than the Commun Biol J44 models (PGS004466/PGS004536) which only report an OR without PRS-only discrimination metrics and have unknown covariates. Main limitation: evidence is not decisive because PGS001788 is also a direct COPD PRS-CS-auto model from the same publication family with much larger validation size, and several candidates report only partial-r or effect sizes, making cross-model performance comparability imperfect; additionally, PGS001783’s reported R2 slightly exceeds the provided local h2_obs (0.0122), suggesting possible scale/definition mismatch and lowering certainty.

Among the 6 direct-match candidates, PGS004621 has the cleanest alignment to the target trait (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both "cirrhosis") and is supported by a large, disease-focused multi-cohort development/validation context (training_development_cohorts lists multiple biobanks; validation_sample_size n=1,153,995) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Structurally it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with broad variant coverage (1,089,806 variants), which is generally favorable for complex traits when endpoint fidelity is good. The main limitation is that the reported discrimination is a full-model AUROC (0.68) rather than an explicitly PRS-only metric, making cross-model performance comparisons uncertain; however, competing cirrhosis-of-liver models either have much sparser variant sets (e.g., 12 SNPs in PGS000726) or have endpoint/subtype mismatches toward alcohol-related cirrhosis (PGS000704/PGS001777/PGS004913) or ambiguous phenotype wording (PGS000776), so PGS004621 is the best-supported direct match from the visible metadata.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency

decision.rationale: Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034), both mapped to the same target EFO term and with identical reported/phenotyped endpoint text (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”), same publication family (UKB portability framework), similar covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and the same validation context (selected European validation; n=19,864). Reported PRS-comparable performance is limited to partial correlation and is essentially identical between the two (partial-r 0.0562 vs 0.0563), with no AUC/R2/effect sizes to further separate them. Given indistinguishable endpoint and metric evidence, the main differentiator is structural: PGS002034 uses LDpred2 with far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is a supportive signal for capturing more polygenic signal when other evidence is tied. However, because both models come from a portability/pan-trait framework paper and lack stronger PRS-only metrics (AUC/R2) or effect sizes, the overall direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence.

Both candidates are direct matches for the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all state corneal dystrophy) and come from the same UKB portability publication with the same training cohort (UKB), similar covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and the same validation sample size and ancestry distribution. With endpoint fidelity and study context effectively tied, the main differentiators are method/performance: PGS002042 uses LDpred2 with far more variants (59,944 vs 38) and shows a higher reported partial correlation in the selected European validation record (0.0471 vs 0.0384), which is supportive of stronger PRS signal. Confidence is not high because neither model reports standard PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 (only partial-r is provided), and both are from a portability/framework-style study rather than a disease-focused multi-cohort corneal dystrophy effort.

Direct-match CAD candidates are abundant (85). Among the visible set, PGS003725 is a strong direct CAD endpoint match (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all coronary artery disease) from a disease-focused Nat Med study explicitly aiming to improve CAD prediction, with multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/MAE/SAS) and strong per-SD effect sizes (HR=1.75; OR=2.14), supporting meaningful PRS signal. However, the context provides no clearly PRS-only discrimination metric (e.g., PGS-only AUROC/R2) for PGS003725, and several other direct CAD models report high full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS001780 AUROC 0.913 but with questionnaire-risk integration; PGS000018 AUROC 0.89 but prevalent endpoint and small validation n=3,309; PGS000013 AUROC 0.81 with some PRS-only R2=0.04). Because full-model AUROC is often covariate-driven and endpoints/covariates differ across candidates, the evidence does not uniquely identify a single clearly superior model, so confidence is moderate and the overall direct-match recommendation is sub-optimal rather than high-quality.

All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align). PGS001330 is a time-to-event endpoint, which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty for a generic Crohn’s disease risk target. Between the two near-clone snpnet models from the same pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (a known weaker study archetype for external generalization), PGS001331 has slightly stronger PRS-comparable metrics than PGS001330 (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R² 0.00677 vs 0.00621; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) with essentially identical basic covariates and validation context, making it the better-supported pick within that family. PGS004254 reports a much higher full-model AUROC (0.72) and an OR (2.18), but it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R² and its performance evidence is therefore not directly comparable to the snpnet models per the provided guidance; additionally, its publication context is not clearly a Crohn’s-disease-focused PRS development paper from the visible metadata. Overall, a direct-match exists, but the best choice remains sub-optimal because the leading candidate comes from a pan-trait framework family and the strongest-looking alternative has non-comparable (full-model-only) discrimination reporting.

Direct-match dementia candidates are present (e.g., PGS000929/PGS000946/PGS001827/PGS002035/PGS004281–PGS004284/PGS004318/PGS005170). PGS005170 is best supported because its phenotype is explicitly aligned to the target ("Incident all-cause dementia"; trait_efo=dementia) and it uses an integrative multi-PRS approach ("integrative PRS of 24 component PRSs"), which the provided domain guidance flags as a strong structural positive signal versus single-score constructions. It also reports a direct discrimination metric (AUROC=0.761) and an effect size (HR=1.25, 95% CI 1.11–1.42) in European validation. Main limitation: several other direct-match dementia models report higher full-model AUROC values (e.g., PGS000946 full_model_auc=0.835; PGS004281 full_model_auc≈0.819), but these are from framework/single-biobank contexts (snpnet UKB) or are full-model metrics without clear PRS-only comparability; given the domain guidance to discount framework scores and to avoid substituting full-model AUROC for PRS-only performance, this leaves some residual uncertainty, hence Moderate confidence.

Direct-match candidates for depressive disorder are present (multiple models mapped to depressive disorder / major depressive disorder). Among these, PGS003578 is the most supported on endpoint fidelity and comparable performance: it targets lifetime major depressive disorder (trait_efo: major depressive disorder; phenotyping_reported: major depressive disorder) and reports one of the higher variance-explained values in this direct-match set (R²=0.0257) with basic covariate adjustment (PCs 1–10) and a reasonably large European validation sample (n=42,250). Competing direct matches either have weaker reported R²/AUROC (e.g., the 2020 UKB minimal-phenotyping clumping scores with full-model AUROC ~0.53–0.56 and lower R²), are framework/portability-style scores with weaker partial-correlation metrics (PGS001829/PGS002036), or have endpoint/context mismatches (e.g., antidepressant side-effect phenotype; brain imaging phenotype). Limitation: the selected model’s reported metric is not explicitly PRS-only (and several near-sibling models from the same preprint family have very similar endpoints and close R² values), so the evidence does not uniquely identify a single clearly superior direct-match model, keeping confidence below high.

All 8 candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, with generally acceptable endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported includes dilated cardiomyopathy; several are explicitly non-ischemic DCM or clinical DCM). Domain guidance mildly prefers MTAG-enhanced siblings within the same study family when endpoints are otherwise aligned. Among the two 2024-04-18 Nat Genet siblings with identical evaluation ancestry (EUR), covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10), and validation size (n=347,585), PGS004862 (MTAG) shows slightly stronger reported performance/effect size than PGS004861 (full-model AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; R² 0.05 vs 0.048; OR 1.76 vs 1.56), making it the best-supported pick within that coherent pair. However, confidence is limited because across the full candidate set most metrics are full-model (not PRS-only), covariate sets differ across studies, and some later-release models report unusually large liability-scale R² values without clear PRS-only comparability, making cross-model ranking uncertain from the provided metadata alone.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to diverticular disease (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align on diverticular disease/K57, with one including diverticulitis). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, PGS000997 (snpnet; TTE diverticular disease of intestine) shows stronger PRS-only performance than the sibling framework score PGS000996 (PGS-only AUROC 0.591 vs 0.552; PGS-only R² 0.0178 vs 0.0037; higher incremental AUROC 0.0173 vs 0.0084), and its PRS-only R² is consistent with the provided heritability sanity-check context. The newer disease-focused candidates (PGS004614/PGS004474/PGS004544) have appealing study context and/or effect sizes, but they lack PRS-only metrics in the visible metadata; additionally, PGS004614’s reported AUROC (0.76) is a full-model metric with family history/age/sex covariates, which is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance. Therefore PGS000997 is the best-supported choice from the available evidence, but confidence is limited because the strongest disease-focused 2024 models cannot be fairly ranked without PRS-only metrics and covariate-comparable validation details.

All three candidates are direct matches for the target trait (all map to EFO: Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported is Dupuytren’s disease / contracture of palmar fascia). PGS001254 reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.6646; PGS R² 0.0247) but comes from a pan-trait sparse UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus more disease-focused constructions. PGS001880 and PGS002092 come from the same UKB portability study family with identical endpoint/covariates and provide comparable PRS signal via partial correlation; between them, PGS002092 is slightly better supported on the visible performance metric (partial-r 0.0797 vs 0.0783) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (484,484 vs 2,443), a structural positive signal when endpoints are the same. Limitation: the portability-study models do not report PRS-only AUROC/R² here (only partial-r), and all candidates are UKB-derived framework/portability archetypes rather than clearly disease-consortium multi-cohort scores, so the best choice remains somewhat uncertain.

All four candidates map to the target EFO (follicular lymphoma), but endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence are limited/uneven. PGS000643 and PGS000644 are coherent siblings (same publication, EUR-only, same training/validation sizes, basic covariates age/sex/batch/PCs) with consistent phenotype labeling as “Nodular lymphoma,” which aligns with follicular (nodular) lymphoma; however, they report only full-model AUROC (0.532–0.538) and small pseudo-R², so PRS-only performance is not directly supported. PGS002304 has the exact reported trait (“Follicular lymphoma”) and higher full-model AUROC (0.61) but is a 6-variant GWAS-hits score with very small validation (n=197) and unknown covariates, making the apparent AUROC hard to interpret and less robust. PGS003455 has an internal metadata conflict (phenotyping_reported = chronic lymphocytic leukemia despite trait_reported = follicular lymphoma) and no AUROC/R², so endpoint fidelity is questionable. Between the two PRSweb siblings, evidence does not clearly separate them; PGS000643 is selected only because it shows a stronger reported top-1% vs rest OR (2.49 vs 1.48) under otherwise similar design, but the lack of PRS-only metrics keeps confidence low.

All 15 candidates are direct matches to glaucoma or its dominant clinical subtype primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Several are framework-style UK Biobank pan-trait/portability scores (PGS001321/PGS001322/PGS001323; PGS001836; PGS002043) which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models despite having tidy PRS-only metrics (e.g., modest PGS-only AUROC ~0.60 and small PGS-only R2). Among the disease-focused POAG candidates, PGS001792 (PRS-CS-auto; Cell Genom 2022) has strong structural properties (genome-wide shrinkage; ~911k variants), very large validation (n=347,396), and a high reported full-model AUROC (0.777) with only basic demographic/PC covariates, making it the best-supported direct-match choice in this context. However, confidence is limited because most candidates (including PGS001792) lack clearly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R2 across the pool, and some reported AUROCs are full-model (covariate-influenced) rather than isolating PRS contribution; additionally, another disease-focused candidate (PGS000137) reports an even higher full-model AUROC (0.8) but includes family history as a covariate, complicating comparability.

Multiple direct-match gout PRS candidates are present. PGS001789 is best supported overall because it is a genome-wide shrinkage score (PRS-CS-auto; 910,151 variants) developed from a large multi-biobank, multi-ancestry GWAS context (many contributing cohorts listed) with a very large validation sample (n=359,345) and reports PRS-comparable signal (Nagelkerke’s R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.031208), which is below the provided gout liability heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.0525) and therefore passes the heritability sanity check. Competing candidates either come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., PGS001248/PGS001249 from the ‘813 traits’ paper; PGS001822/PGS002030 from the ‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores’ paper) or report only full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS004265–PGS004269), making their discrimination less comparable. Limitation: the selected validation ancestry for PGS001789 is European despite multi-ancestry GWAS/evaluation strings, and several other gout models show similar full-model AUROC values; because PRS-only AUROC is not available for most candidates, the choice relies on indirect comparability (PRS-only R2 availability + study archetype) rather than a clean head-to-head PRS-only discrimination comparison.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported = lymphocytic thyroiditis) and come from the same publication family with the same evaluation ancestry grouping and the same validation sample size (n=94,651), so endpoint fidelity and transportability context do not differentiate them. None reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; only full-model AUROC is shown, which domain guidance says should not be used as the primary ranking signal, lowering overall certainty. Given the lack of PRS-comparable metrics, the strongest differentiator available is effect size magnitude and structural method properties: PGS005271 (PRSCS; ~1.085M variants) has the strongest per-SD effect size (OR≈1.55) among the three, consistent with stronger PRS signal, while also using a genome-wide shrinkage method versus the sparse P+T model (PGS005270). PGS005272 is also PRSCS but has weaker full-model AUROC and weaker OR than PGS005271. Remaining limitation: covariates are unknown and the reported AUROCs are full-model, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be verified from the provided metadata.

Multiple direct-match candidates for heart failure are present. PGS005097 is preferred because it is a disease-focused, multi-cohort heart-failure PRS (publication explicitly on heart failure genetic architecture; training cohorts include multiple major HF resources such as HERMES and MVP plus several biobanks), uses a modern cross-ancestry shrinkage method (PRS-CSx) with genome-wide variant coverage (1,274,692 variants), and reports a reasonably strong discrimination metric in validation (full-model AUROC=0.72 with Brier skill score reported). Main limitation: across the candidate set, PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC or clearly PRS-only R2) are largely absent; the AUROC reported here is a full-model metric and covariates differ/are sometimes unknown across studies, so comparative ranking remains uncertain. Competing models show similar or higher full-model C-index (~0.753 in the MVP CHF PheCode benchmarking set) but are for congestive heart failure (not identical to generic HF) and likewise lack PRS-only metrics, leaving no clearly decisive winner.

All 7 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (hip osteoarthritis / coxarthrosis / hip OA-related endpoints), but the evidence is heterogeneous and often lacks PRS-comparable metrics. PGS002763 has the cleanest endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: "Hip osteoarthritis") and provides a reasonably strong PRS-only discriminative signal via an effect size (OR=1.38 per SD, 95% CI 1.31–1.46) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical), and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (~1.05M), which is structurally favorable for a polygenic trait. Competing models have notable limitations: PGS000967 is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits") and its strong full-model AUROC is largely covariate-driven (incremental AUROC 0.00918; PGS-only R2 0.00628), while PGS002728/PGS002750 use hip replacement/total hip replacement proxies rather than OA diagnosis and have limited/absent PRS-only metrics; PGS004478/PGS004548 have unknown covariates and only single-point ORs; PGS004882 is incident-only and has an unusually small training n (404) despite large evaluation, with only a full-model C-index reported. Because no candidate provides a clearly superior, directly comparable PRS-only AUC/R2 on the same endpoint, the selection remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence.

Direct-match Hodgkin lymphoma candidates are present (PGS000637/PGS000638/PGS000639/PGS000640 and PGS003449). Among the Cancer PRSweb Hodgkin’s disease sibling set with consistent phenotype alignment (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both Hodgkin’s disease; EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL; basic covariates age/sex/batch/PCs), PGS000639 (P+T, 20 variants) has the strongest visible validation performance and effect-size evidence: full-model AUROC 0.62 (vs 0.601/0.574/0.569 for the other siblings) and per-SD OR 1.476 (vs 1.377/1.30/1.292). PGS003449 is also a direct-label Hodgkin lymphoma model, but its phenotyping_reported appears inconsistent (listed as chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and it lacks comparable discrimination metrics, making it less coherently supported in this context. Limitation: all Hodgkin candidates here report only full-model AUROC (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R²), and the validation sample sizes are small (e.g., n=775 for the PRSweb models), so the evidence is insufficient to call a clearly high-quality winner despite PGS000639 being the best-supported within the coherent direct-match cluster.

Direct-match hypertension candidates are present (e.g., PGS000706, PGS001320, PGS001838, PGS002047, PGS004191–PGS004194, PGS004234, PGS004236, PGS004934, PGS004785/PGS004787, PGS005144/PGS005153). Among these, PGS004236 is best supported by the visible evidence because it targets hypertension directly (trait_efo=hypertension; phenotyping_reported=prevalent hypertension) and is from a disease-focused hypertension study with explicit multi-ethnic development/validation context (BioMe/MVP/UKB; evaluation described as European, African American or Afro-Caribbean, Hispanic or Latin American, Asian unspecified) and strong reported discrimination evidence for the PRS contribution (effect size OR=2.1, 95% CI 1.99–2.21) alongside a high full-model AUROC (0.764). Competing direct-match options either come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., PGS001320; PGS001838/PGS002047; ExPRSweb series) with weaker or less comparable metrics, have weaker reported discrimination (e.g., PGS000706 AUROC 0.623; PGS004934 OR 1.42), or lack comparable PRS-only metrics and/or have narrower ancestry evaluation. Main limitation: PGS004236 does not report explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 (the AUROC shown is full-model with multiple covariates including BMI and smoking), so cross-model comparability of performance is imperfect and confidence is reduced despite strong endpoint alignment and multi-ethnic validation.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target hyperthyroidism spectrum (thyrotoxicosis/hyperthyroidism and Graves’ disease; domain knowledge explicitly notes Graves’ disease as the dominant autoimmune form of clinical hyperthyroidism). Among candidates, PGS005265 is from a disease-focused global multi-ancestry biobank study family (many contributing cohorts) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count (1,085,173), plus it reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.625), which domain guidance treats as meaningful evidence of PRS discriminative power. The main limitation is that its reported discrimination is only a full-model AUROC (0.665) with unknown covariates and no PGS-only AUROC/R², making performance comparability uncertain; meanwhile the UKB pan-trait snpnet models (PGS001042/PGS001043) do provide explicit PGS-only metrics but come from a framework paper that domain guidance warns often generalizes poorly, and their PRS-only R² (~0.022) is modest. This leaves a preferred choice (PGS005265) but with residual uncertainty due to missing PRS-only metrics and unclear covariate context.

All four candidates are direct matches to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and PRS-relevant evidence. PGS004910 and PGS004911 (same 2025 Nat Genet publication) have clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10), and genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) with ~374k variants, which is structurally favorable for a polygenic disease. Between these siblings, PGS004911 is mildly preferred because it is the MTAG-enhanced version (domain guidance: MTAG is a legitimate power boost and is mildly preferred within the same study family) and it shows stronger reported validation metrics in the provided record (full-model AUROC 0.8 vs 0.73; R² 0.048 vs 0.031; higher HR/OR). PGS000739 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.821) but uses a much heavier clinical covariate set (multiple clinical risk factors plus rare-variant carrier status), making that AUROC less comparable to PRS performance; it also uses only 27 genome-wide significant variants. PGS000778 has a restricted phenotype (clinical events among pathogenic sarcomeric variant carriers) and very small validation (n=368), making it less aligned to general HCM risk. Main limitation: the reported AUROC/R² for PGS004911 appear to be full-model metrics (not explicitly PGS-only), so confidence is reduced despite strong endpoint alignment and favorable method/structure.

Direct-match candidates for hypothyroidism are present (multiple models with trait_efo=hypothyroidism). Among these, PGS004935 is the best-supported on the visible evidence because it targets generic hypothyroidism (phenotyping_reported: "Hypothyroidism"), reports a directly comparable discrimination metric (full_model AUROC=0.70) and a reasonably strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.5, 95% CI 1.41–1.6), with EUR development and EUR evaluation. Key limitation: many candidates lack PRS-only (no-covariates) metrics, and PGS004935’s covariates are listed as "Unknown", so the AUROC may not reflect PRS-only performance; additionally, a newer disease-focused model (PGS005218) reports much higher AUROC (0.859) but uses thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO) as covariates, making that AUROC non-comparable for standalone PRS ranking. This leaves moderate confidence rather than high.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001823, PGS002031), both aligned to the target via trait_efo=iron metabolism disease and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported='Disorders of iron metabolism', with similar UKB-only development, similar covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and identical evaluation/validation context. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC or R2; the only visible performance signal is partial correlation, which is slightly higher for PGS002031 (partial-r 0.1355, CI 0.1219–0.1492) than PGS001823 (0.1307, CI 0.117–0.1444), making PGS002031 the marginally better-supported choice. However, both models come from a UKB portability framework paper and the partial-r confidence intervals overlap, so the evidence is not strong enough for a high-confidence pick.

All four candidates are disease-focused scores from the same publication family (Ann Rheum Dis; SparSNP; EUR-only development and evaluation; similar basic covariates: sex + PCs), so the key differentiator is phenotype alignment to the target trait (juvenile idiopathic arthritis, broadly defined) rather than small differences in full-model AUROC. PGS000114 is the only model whose trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are the generic juvenile idiopathic arthritis endpoint, making it the most direct match for the target. The other three models (PGS000324/325/326) are subtype-specific JIA endpoints (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarthritis) and therefore are less aligned to a broad JIA target despite sometimes higher reported full-model AUROC. Confidence is Moderate because the available performance evidence is primarily full-model AUROC (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), which domain guidance cautions against over-interpreting for PRS-only quality.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to kidney cancer (or near-synonymous renal carcinoma / renal cell carcinoma; RCC is noted in the provided domain knowledge as the dominant subtype of kidney cancer). Among them, PGS004908 has the strongest visible PRS-relevant performance evidence in a large European evaluation (AUROC 0.74, OR per SD 1.5 [1.43–1.58], n=324,805) with phenotype reported as kidney cancer and covariates that are standard risk-model adjustments (age, sex, PCs, BMI, smoking, hypertension). Competing direct-match models either show weaker discrimination (e.g., AUROC ~0.52–0.57 for PGS000605/000606/000722/004690), lack comparable discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS000161/003744/004245), or report similar full-model AUROC (~0.722 for PGS000076/000787) but with weaker per-SD effect sizes (HR ~1.15–1.16) and without PRS-only metrics, making them less compelling than the stronger OR signal in PGS004908. Main limitation: across the pool, reported AUROCs are full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), so comparability is imperfect and confidence is moderated despite PGS004908’s consistent endpoint alignment and stronger effect size.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (kidney failure) are present, notably PGS000708 (trait_reported: Kidney failure; phenotyping: diabetic kidney failure) and the N18 chronic renal failure models PGS004492/PGS004562 (trait_efo: kidney failure; phenotyping: N18 chronic renal failure). Among these, PGS004492 is the most endpoint-aligned to generic kidney failure (chronic renal failure) without an explicit restriction to a diabetic subtype, whereas PGS000708 is explicitly restricted to diabetic kidney failure. However, the evidence is insufficient for a high-quality recommendation because PGS004492 reports no PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R²; no full-model AUROC) and has unknown covariates, limiting interpretability and comparability; PGS004562 shows a stronger OR (1.395) but is otherwise similarly underspecified, making the choice between the two N18 models not decisively supported by the visible metadata.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to knee osteoarthritis (trait_efo aligns; several explicitly report knee OA/gonarthrosis). PGS002767 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: "Knee osteoarthritis") and provides a clear PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD = 1.35, 95% CI 1.30–1.40) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,052,275 variants) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical covariates), which is generally more informative for standalone PRS quality than full-model AUROC values. Key limitation: most candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R², and the only model with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS001192) comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores despite having well-formatted metrics; meanwhile PGS002729 reports only a covariate-including full-model AUROC (age/sex/BMI) without PRS-only metrics, making cross-model performance comparison uncertain. Therefore a direct match exists but the evidence is insufficient for a high-confidence, clearly best-supported choice.

All 5 candidates are direct matches at the trait_efo level (late-onset Alzheimer’s disease), but the evidence is not strong enough to declare a single clearly superior, high-quality winner because PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are largely missing and several candidates have endpoint/covariate ambiguities. PGS000054 and PGS000053 are the most endpoint-faithful (familial late-onset AD) and report interpretable per-SD effect sizes; among them, PGS000054 shows a stronger OR per SD (1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) than PGS000053 (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.21–1.37), which is supportive of better PRS signal. However, PGS000054 is evaluated in AMR (Hispanic/Latin American) rather than EUR, while other candidates are EUR-evaluated; additionally, other models either report only full-model metrics (e.g., PGS004918 AUROC 0.731 with unknown covariates) or have suspect/non-comparable metrics (PGS000334 reports R²=0.191 from C+T with unknown covariates, which is difficult to interpret and potentially inflated). These limitations keep confidence moderate and the overall outcome sub-optimal despite the presence of direct matches.

Direct-match candidates for lung cancer are present (multiple models with trait_reported/phenotyping_reported as lung cancer or closely overlapping lung/bronchus cancer). PGS000078 is best supported in the visible evidence because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: incident lung cancer; trait_efo: lung carcinoma), very large European evaluation (n=392,539; EUR-only GWAS/EVAL), and reports a per-SD effect size (HR=1.16, 95% CI 1.11–1.22) alongside discrimination metrics (AUROC 0.846; C-index 0.849). Main limitation: the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with extensive covariates (including family history, PM2.5, and detailed smoking terms/interactions), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided; therefore the apparent performance advantage may be substantially covariate-driven, lowering certainty versus other direct-match options (e.g., PGS004860 with high AUROC but also only full-model metrics, and several smaller/covariate-heavy lung cancer scores).

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus (both EFO:lupus erythematosus and systemic lupus erythematosus). Among models with a clear SLE diagnosis endpoint, PGS000328 shows relatively strong reported discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.83 in European evaluation; n=1,001) compared with other diagnosis-anchored SLE models like PGS000196 (AUROC=0.79; n=245) and PGS004917 (AUROC=0.696). Several other candidates are endpoint-mismatched for a generic lupus erythematosus target (renal disease/onset: PGS000771/PGS000772; lupus nephritis/criteria counts: PGS003755/PGS003756; broad ‘erythematous conditions’: PGS000803) or come from a portability framework with weak partial-correlation metrics (PGS001870/PGS002082). However, confidence is limited because the available AUROCs are full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), covariates are unknown for key candidates (including PGS000328), and PGS003960 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.89) but is explicitly adjusted with a ‘phenotype risk score’ covariate (non-genetic packaging), making its metric non-comparable for standalone PRS ranking.

Direct-match candidates for the target EFO (lymphoid leukemia) are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). PGS000077 is preferred because its phenotyping_reported is a direct endpoint aligned to the target concept (Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia), it uses a reasonably sized GWAS-significant variant set (75 variants), and it reports supportive effect-size evidence (HR=1.45 per SD, 95% CI 1.31–1.61) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), reducing concern about covariate-driven inflation. However, confidence is not high because none of the candidates provide clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 are null), and competing direct-match models exist with similar endpoint framing and slightly higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000788) but with unclear PRS comparability (full-model metrics only), making the best choice somewhat uncertain from the visible metadata alone.

All 7 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (macular degeneration / age-related macular degeneration), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality. PGS004606 is best supported because it is disease-focused with a clean, direct clinical endpoint (phenotyping_reported: "Age-related macular degeneration"), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant coverage (~1,000,946), and reports a full-model AUROC of 0.71 plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.76, 95% CI 1.73–1.78) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Competing models are weaker on visible evidence: PGS001013 is a pan-trait UKB sparse framework score with low PGS-only AUROC (~0.553) and small PGS-only R2 (~0.006); PGS001834/PGS002041 are UKB portability-framework scores with only small partial correlations (~0.016–0.018) and no AUC/R2; PGS002269 has phenotype mismatch (retinal layer thickness proxy) and only a beta; PGS004607 is an AFR-GWAS-derived sibling with lower reported AUROC (0.65) and weaker OR (1.48); PGS004952 reports an implausibly formatted AUROC (listed as 84.2) on a small validation sample (n=1,232) and targets late AMD specifically, making its performance evidence hard to interpret from the provided metadata. Main limitation: PGS004606 lacks explicit PRS-only (no-covariate) discrimination metrics in the context, so confidence is reduced despite strong endpoint/method/effect-size support.

Multiple direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (e.g., PGS000079, PGS000118, PGS000732, PGS000743, PGS000766, PGS000790, PGS000813, PGS002246/PGS002247, PGS003430, PGS004247, PGS005208). Among these, PGS000813 is a direct melanoma model (trait_efo=melanoma; phenotyping_reported=familial cutaneous melanoma in non-carriers of CDKN2A) with strong reported discrimination (full_model AUROC=0.77, 95% CI 0.75–0.79) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR=2.12, 95% CI 1.9–2.35), which is supportive evidence of meaningful PRS signal. Competing direct-match models either show weaker reported discrimination (e.g., PGS000118 full_model AUROC=0.61; PGS000732 full_model AUROC=0.579; PGS002246/PGS002247 full_model AUROC ~0.69) or have performance that is less directly comparable due to heavier covariate packaging (e.g., PGS000743 includes many traditional risk factors) or lack comparable metrics. Main limitation: PGS000813’s endpoint is a restricted familial melanoma subset (non-carriers of CDKN2A), so general-population melanoma risk performance is not fully established from the provided metadata; this endpoint specificity lowers confidence despite strong effect-size and AUROC evidence.

All six candidates are nominal direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (multiple myeloma / plasma cell myeloma), but one (PGS003450) has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported = Chronic lymphocytic leukemia), making it weaker for a direct-match choice despite the trait fields. Among the remaining coherent multiple-myeloma endpoints, PGS002281 provides the strongest support from the visible evidence: it reports the highest full-model AUROC (0.644; 95% CI 0.622–0.666) on a moderate European validation sample (n=2,395) with basic covariates (age, sex, geographic region). Competing PRSweb models (PGS000652/653/654) have substantially lower full-model AUROC (~0.55–0.58) and modest per-SD ORs (~1.24–1.33), while PGS002306 shows a higher AUROC (0.69) but on a much smaller validation sample (n=290) and with unknown covariates, reducing comparability. Confidence is only Moderate and outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because none of the candidates report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so the reported AUROCs are full-model and not strictly comparable across differing covariate sets, limiting a high-quality direct recommendation.

All 7 listed candidates are direct matches to multiple sclerosis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, but the evidence is mixed and often not PRS-comparable (many report only full-model metrics or partial-r). PGS000809 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused MS study (not a pan-trait/portability framework paper) with a clear MS endpoint and basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and it provides some performance evidence (full-model AUROC 0.765; R² 0.069; plus an effect size β=0.63) in a European evaluation. Key limitation: its reported AUROC is full-model (not PGS-only), so PRS-only discrimination cannot be directly compared across candidates; meanwhile the only candidates with explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS001270/PGS001271) are from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper that domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation. Other disease-focused-looking options (e.g., PGS002726 with AUROC 0.8, OR top 10% vs median 15.0) have very small validation (n=938) and unknown covariates, and the UKB portability scores (PGS001831/PGS002038) provide only partial-r without AUC/R², leaving no clearly dominant choice.

Multiple direct-match myocardial infarction PRS candidates are present (e.g., PGS000710; PGS001314/PGS001315/PGS001316/PGS001317; PGS004458/PGS004528; PGS005034–PGS005046). The strongest direct endpoint alignment is provided by models explicitly mapped to myocardial infarction with matching phenotyping (e.g., PGS005039: trait_reported “Myocardial infarction (PheCode 411.2)”, trait_efo “myocardial infarction”, phenotyping_reported “Myocardial infarction”). Among these, PGS005039 has the best visible comparable discrimination metric (C-index 0.784836989151752 in European validation) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.578, 95% CI 1.50–1.67), supporting meaningful PRS signal. Competing direct-match models from the UKB pan-trait sparse framework (PGS001314–PGS001317) are penalized by the framework context despite reporting PGS-only metrics, and the Commun Biol acute MI models (PGS004458/PGS004528) have unknown covariates and lack comparable AUC/R2, limiting interpretability. Overall confidence is reduced because many MI candidates are near-ties within the same 2024 MVP comparison family (PGS005035/PGS005038/PGS005041/PGS005044/PGS005045/PGS005046 have very similar C-index/OR), and the context does not provide external (non-European) performance to separate them.

Both candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = Nasal Cavity Polyp; phenotyping_reported = ICD10 J33 Nasal polyp) and come from the same publication, with identical EUR-only development/evaluation context, training cohort (UKB), training size, variant count, and validation sample size—so endpoint fidelity and transportability do not differentiate them. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (all null), leaving limited comparable performance evidence; however, PGS004535 reports a stronger per-SD effect size (OR=1.600668) than PGS004465 (OR=1.3496), which is supportive for better discrimination when other evidence is otherwise indistinguishable.
